answer: Rate limiting makes sybil identities cheap to create but useless to deploy: a brand-new identity may cast one vote per day, like a narrow dawn trail that admits a single hiker at a time — a thousand fake hikers then need a thousand days. Quota grows only with age and vouched history, so an attacker must pay in time itself: it cannot be minted, bought in bulk, or forged. New agents sit in a small oasis of permission while the old guard of timber quotas decides big moves; the attack surface shrinks from infinite clones to the single dimension of waiting.
